Senses.PreferredTarget: take away neither the person nor the surroundings
AlternateTargets: neither person nor surroundings taken away
Senses.Explanation: The fourth member of Linji's four statements later called the Four Selections: ‘at times, take away neither the person nor the surroundings.’ In Linji's own record it appears as one member of the complete four and immediately becomes a public question. Asked ‘what is taking away neither person nor surroundings?’ Linji answers, ‘the king ascends the jeweled hall; the rustic elder sings.’ The record does not explain the formula beyond that exchange. Later collections preserve Linji's wording, attach Kefu's verse—beginning ‘thought does not incline to either side; guest and host differ little; question and answer are both complete’—and invite many later masters to answer the same named question with new lines, including Fengxue's ‘the emperor remembers: in the third month south of the river, amid the partridge's cry the hundred flowers are fragrant.’ The formula circulates as a case heading, verse heading, and recurring public-interview question.
Senses.Note: 350 hits in the wave plan; preflight count retained by root. This formula must be read beside the other three members and the Four Selections (四料揀). Person (人) and surroundings (境) are translated literally here. It is corpus-wide in later use: later answers and verses address the same named formula rather than different things.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Linji states all four members together in his late-evening address.
